text:
Re: Lorna Barker, 67

Mild COPD (FEV1 72% predicted), stable on tiotropium with no exacerbations in 2 years. Breathlessness mMRC 1; she walks her dog daily. Ex-smoker for 10 years. Vaccinations up to date. Meds: tiotropium 18 mcg daily, salbutamol prn, rarely used, and atorvastatin. She has asked about pulmonary rehabilitation and whether she needs any specialist follow-up.

Dr Shane Kirby
note: Mild stable COPD; advice only.

text:
Re: Thomas Brennan, 57, lipid management

Thomas developed myalgia on atorvastatin, rosuvastatin and pravastatin, each rechallenged at low dose. LDL 4.6 off treatment, 3.8 on ezetimibe alone. Lp(a) 210 nmol/L. No known vascular disease; CT calcium score 85 last year. He is asymptomatic, exercises three times a week and does not smoke. He is interested in discussing eligibility for a PCSK9 inhibitor or other lipid-lowering options.

Dr Esther Wilkins
note: Asymptomatic lipid optimisation with statin intolerance; no active cardiac disease.

text:
Dear Dr,

Re: Megan Cho, 27

Megan has generalised epilepsy diagnosed at 16 and has been seizure-free for 6 years on lamotrigine 150 mg bd. She has no side effects and holds a full driver's licence. She is planning a pregnancy in the next couple of years and would like to discuss whether her medication could be reduced or stopped, and pre-conception planning. EEG 2020 normal. Folic acid 5 mg started.

Kind regards,
Dr Grace Ellison
note: Well-controlled epilepsy with planning questions; pregnancy is not imminent.

text:
Re: Aisha Kamara, 30

Left-sided ulcerative colitis diagnosed in 2020 in Perth, in remission on mesalazine 4 g daily for 2 years. Last colonoscopy (2024): mild quiescent disease. Calprotectin last month 40. Normal bowel habit, no bleeding. She has relocated for work and needs ongoing IBD care, including scheduled surveillance. Copies of previous letters enclosed. She is on no other regular medication.

Dr Liam Corcoran
note: Quiescent ulcerative colitis; transfer of care.

text:
Re: Joan Whittaker, 64

Bronchiectasis of both lower lobes on CT, with daily purulent sputum and 4 exacerbations needing antibiotics in the past 12 months. Sputum has grown Pseudomonas aeruginosa twice. She has been taught airway clearance by a physiotherapist and does it twice daily. Between exacerbations she is breathless only on hills. Would appreciate review regarding eradication therapy and long-term management.

Dr Stephen Marr
note: Bronchiectasis with frequent exacerbations and Pseudomonas; needs specialist input but is not acutely unwell.

text:
Dear Dr,

Kerry-Anne Lowe, 47, has had low back pain with left leg pain for 5 weeks after lifting a heavy box, initially managed with physio and analgesia. Over the last 10 days she has developed a foot drop: today ankle dorsiflexion is 2/5 (4/5 a fortnight ago), EHL 1/5, with reduced sensation over the dorsum of the foot. Bladder and bowel function normal, saddle sensation intact. MRI: large L4/5 left paracentral disc extrusion compressing the L5 nerve root.

Meds: tapentadol SR 50 mg bd, paracetamol.

Kind regards,
Dr Victor Lam
note: Progressive motor deficit from an L4/5 disc extrusion needs urgent spinal surgical review (no cauda equina features, which would mean ED); hard because the back pain with neurological signs could be read as neurology.

text:
Dear Cardiology Registrar,

Re: Graham Petrakis, 58M

Thank you for seeing Graham, who has a 3 week history of central chest tightness brought on by walking uphill to the train station, settling within a few minutes of rest. No symptoms at rest. He is a current smoker (35 pack-years), has type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 7.9%) and treated hypertension. Father had an MI at 54. Resting ECG today shows sinus rhythm with no acute changes. I have started aspirin 100 mg and a GTN spray, and advised him to call 000 if pain occurs at rest or lasts more than 10 minutes.

Kind regards,
Dr Fiona Lattimore
note: New-onset exertional angina in a high-risk smoker with diabetes needs assessment within 30 days.

text:
Cardiology OPD

Pt: Harold Jenkins, 77
Hx: mild to moderate degenerative mitral regurgitation, last echo 2022. Hypertension, controlled. No AF.
Current: asymptomatic, NYHA I, gardening daily.
O/E: pansystolic murmur at apex 2/6, no oedema, chest clear.
Meds: candesartan 16 mg, rosuvastatin 10 mg.
Request: due for surveillance echo and review. Previously under Dr Mahmood, who has retired.

Dr B. Castellano
note: Surveillance of stable mild-moderate MR in an asymptomatic patient.

text:
Hi,

Mr Rajesh Iyer, 48. Six weeks of numbness starting in both feet and now up to the knees, with tingling in the fingertips for the last fortnight. Unsteady walking in the dark, with one fall. Exam: reduced pinprick to mid-shin, absent ankle reflexes, reduced knee reflexes, mild distal weakness of ankle dorsiflexion bilaterally. B12, folate, HbA1c and TFTs normal. No breathing or swallowing difficulty; I have told him to go to ED if these develop.

Dr Kim Taylor
note: Subacute progressive sensorimotor neuropathy with weakness and falls: a progressive neurological deficit.

text:
Re: Nicole Arendt, 40

Nicole's sister was recently diagnosed with alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency. Nicole has tested as MZ genotype with a level of 0.9 g/L. She is a non-smoker, asymptomatic, with normal spirometry and LFTs. She has two teenage children and wonders whether they should be tested. She would like advice on what this means for her and whether she needs any monitoring.

Dr Bianca Tolhurst
note: Asymptomatic alpha-1 carrier with normal lung function.

text:
Dear Dr Hassan,

Re: Mrs Christine Dowell, 59

Christine has had irritable bowel syndrome since her thirties, with bloating and alternating bowel habit, previously well managed with a low-FODMAP diet and peppermint oil. She would like to revisit dietary strategies and has asked about gut-directed hypnotherapy. In the last 3 months she has noticed her stools are sometimes black, and her Hb has fallen from 128 to 101 with ferritin 9. She takes naproxen most days for her knees. Otherwise well.

Many thanks,
Dr Jeremy Cole
note: New melaena with falling Hb and iron deficiency on daily NSAIDs needs urgent endoscopy; hard because the letter is framed as a stable IBS review.

text:
Dear Neurologist,

Re: Samantha Kyle, 34

Samantha had a witnessed generalised tonic-clonic seizure at home on Sunday morning, lasting about 2 minutes, with tongue biting and post-ictal confusion for 30 minutes. No previous seizures, no alcohol excess or drugs, and she slept normally the night before. ED CT brain and bloods were normal and she was discharged with first seizure advice. Examination today is normal. She drives to work and has been told not to drive. I would be grateful for an urgent appointment, EEG and MRI.

Kind regards,
Dr Andrew Sinclair
note: First unprovoked generalised seizure; the GP's urgent request matches.

text:
Dear Dr,

Mr Leonard Grech, 66, ex-smoker, drinks 3 to 4 beers daily. Two months of food sticking behind the sternum, first with steak and now also with bread and rice; liquids are fine. He has lost 5 kg. Long history of heartburn, self-treated with antacids. No haematemesis. Exam: thin, no lymphadenopathy. Hb 131. Pantoprazole 40 mg started. Would appreciate gastroscopy.

Kind regards,
Dr Sophie Lambert
note: Progressive solid dysphagia with weight loss in an older ex-smoker: suspected oesophageal cancer.

text:
Re: Tim Rowe, 39

His partner complains about his snoring, which is worse after alcohol and when on his back. No witnessed apnoeas. Epworth 5, BMI 27, BP normal. He feels refreshed in the mornings, drinks 2 to 3 beers most nights and has no nasal symptoms. He has asked about a mandibular advancement splint and whether he needs a sleep study.

Dr Penny Sloane
note: Simple snoring without sleepiness or apnoeas.

text:
Dear Neurologist,

Mr Walter Brandt, 72, retired engineer. Over the past year his wife has noticed a tremor of his left hand at rest, his handwriting has become smaller and he shuffles slightly. Exam: left-sided rest tremor, cogwheel rigidity, bradykinesia and reduced arm swing. No falls, cognition normal, no hallucinations. Not on antipsychotics or metoclopramide. He is managing day to day but would like a diagnosis and treatment plan.

Kind regards,
Dr Moira Quinn
note: Probable new Parkinson's disease without falls or cognitive change; needs diagnosis within months.

text:
Re: Agnes Kirby, 75

Agnes has mild, flexible hammer toes of the 2nd and 3rd toes on the right foot. There is occasional rubbing in closed shoes, managed with toe props and wider shoes recommended by her podiatrist. No ulceration, foot pulses good, not diabetic. She would like an orthopaedic opinion on whether anything further should be done.

Kind regards,
Dr Leo Fischer
note: Mild flexible hammer toes managed conservatively; minimal dysfunction.

text:
Re: Geoffrey Tan, 58

Mild right knee OA on X-ray (2023). Occasional ache after long walks, settled with paracetamol. Full range of movement, no effusion, stable ligaments. No change over the last two years. He is a keen golfer and plays 18 holes weekly. He has asked for a specialist opinion on whether he will eventually need a knee replacement and what he can do to protect the joint.

Dr Ananya Bose
note: Stable mild osteoarthritis with minimal pain or dysfunction.

text:
Dear Dr,

Re: Mohammed Ali Rahimi, 49

Mohammed presented 4 months ago with burning retrosternal pain, mostly after large meals and on lying down, sometimes with an acid taste. Because of his age and smoking history I referred him to cardiology: ECG, troponin and stress echo were all normal and he has been discharged. Pantoprazole 40 mg daily has helped about half. No dysphagia, weight loss or anaemia. He is still waking at night with pain. Would appreciate gastroscopy and management advice.

Kind regards,
Dr Lena Hargrave
note: Reflux-type chest pain after a negative cardiac work-up, partly PPI-responsive and without alarm features; hard because the chest pain and cardiology history could pull to cardiology.

text:
Dear Respiratory / TB Clinic,

Mr Arjun Mehta, 29, a nurse recently arrived from India, had a positive QuantiFERON on employment screening. He is asymptomatic, with no cough, fever, night sweats or weight loss, and his CXR is normal. HIV negative, LFTs normal, no other medical history and no regular medicines. Would appreciate assessment for treatment of latent tuberculosis infection.

Regards,
Dr Kylie Mason
note: Latent TB with a normal CXR and no symptoms; no active disease.

text:
Sore shoulder.

Joan Edwards, 60. Please assess and manage. She has had pain in the left shoulder for a while and has tried Panadol. Not sure what makes it worse or whether it wakes her.

PMH: hypothyroidism, hypertension.
Meds: thyroxine 100 mcg, perindopril 5 mg.
Allergies: penicillin (rash).
No imaging done yet. Right handed. Lives with husband, independent.

Thanks
Dr R. Keller
note: No duration, red flags or functional impact are given; with nothing concerning described it defaults to routine. Hard because there is almost no clinical detail.

text:
Dear Dr,

Re: Joshua Pereira, 42

Joshua has had papulopustular rosacea for several years, flushing with alcohol and spicy food, and is currently using ivermectin cream with moderate benefit. He would like to discuss oral treatment or laser for the persistent redness. While examining him I also noticed a brown-black streak in his left thumbnail, about 4 mm wide, which he says appeared about 3 months ago and has widened; the pigment extends onto the cuticle. No trauma he can recall.

Kind regards,
Dr Fiona Baird
note: Widening melanonychia with pigment onto the nail fold suggests subungual melanoma; hard because the stated reason for referral is rosacea.

text:
Re: Desmond Albury, 60

Former underground coal miner in Queensland for 20 years. He left the industry 8 years ago. He is asymptomatic, with no cough or breathlessness, and has a normal CXR and normal spirometry. Never smoker. Several former colleagues have been diagnosed with coal workers' pneumoconiosis and he would like specialist assessment and advice on ongoing screening.

Dr Rania Saleh
note: Asymptomatic exposure screening with normal tests.

text:
Re: Isabella Romano, 31

Known bicuspid aortic valve, followed by cardiology in Brisbane until she moved here last year. Last echo (2024): mild aortic regurgitation, no stenosis, aortic root 34 mm. She is asymptomatic and exercises regularly. She is planning a pregnancy in the next year or two and would like her care transferred, with advice on pre-conception assessment. A copy of the previous echo report is attached.

Dr Noor Al-Saadi
note: Stable bicuspid valve with mild AR, transfer of care; pregnancy is not imminent.

text:
Dear Orthopaedic Team,

Ms Kirra Simpson, 23, university student, has a 1 year history of a small lump on the back of the left wrist. It is painless, fluctuates in size and causes no numbness. Ultrasound: 12 mm ganglion arising from the scapholunate joint. She finds it cosmetically bothersome and would like to discuss excision. Full wrist function; she plays guitar without difficulty. No relevant past history.

Kind regards,
Dr Felicity Hume
note: Painless ganglion with full function; cosmetic concern only.

text:
Re: Bernard Lim, 74

Moderate aortic stenosis first noted in 2023 (Vmax 3.2 m/s). Repeat echo this month shows progression: Vmax 3.7 m/s, mean gradient 34 mmHg, AVA 1.1 cm2, LVEF normal. He denies chest pain, syncope or breathlessness and still walks 5 km most mornings. Examination: ejection systolic murmur 3/6, normal second heart sound. Would be grateful for review regarding surveillance and the likely timing of intervention.

Many thanks,
Dr Carla Benedetti
note: Progressing but asymptomatic moderate aortic stenosis needs specialist review within months; symptoms would make it urgent.

text:
Dear Dr,

Thank you for seeing Alan Pemberton, 62, retired electrician. A pre-operative ECG for his hernia repair showed right bundle branch block, which was not present on an ECG from 2017. He is entirely asymptomatic: no syncope, presyncope, palpitations or breathlessness, and walks 10 km a week. Echo: structurally normal heart. His hernia surgery went ahead uneventfully. I would appreciate your opinion as to whether any further follow-up is required.

Regards,
Dr Ruth Kemp
note: Isolated new RBBB in an asymptomatic man with a normal echo is low risk.

text:
Re: Lucy Abara, 38

Long-standing bilateral pressing headaches for many years, 6 to 8 days a month, mild to moderate, without nausea or photophobia, and related to stress and screen time. Simple analgesia on about 4 days a month. No change in pattern, no neurological symptoms, normal exam and fundi. She has started physio for neck posture. She is keen to see a specialist to confirm nothing else is going on.

Dr Peter Lindqvist
note: Long-standing unchanged tension-type headache with a normal exam.

text:
Re: Geoff Barnard, 63

A private colonoscopy 3 years ago removed two tubular adenomas (8 mm and 12 mm, low-grade dysplasia, completely excised), with surveillance recommended at 3 years. He is asymptomatic, bowel habit normal, Hb 145. He takes aspirin 100 mg for primary prevention. No family history of bowel cancer. He can no longer afford private care and would like surveillance through the public clinic.

Dr Anna Kostas
note: Scheduled post-polypectomy surveillance in an asymptomatic man.

text:
Dear Dr Sandhu,

Re: Peter Albrechtsen, 63

Peter is a long-standing patient with hypertension and hyperlipidaemia. His BP has been variable (home average 148/92) despite perindopril 10 mg and amlodipine 10 mg, and his LDL remains 3.4 on atorvastatin 40 mg, which he says gives him leg aches. He mentioned that twice in the last fortnight he had a heavy feeling across his chest while carrying shopping up his steep driveway, easing after he stopped. He otherwise feels well and is keen to discuss alternatives to his statin. ECG unchanged from last year.

I'd appreciate your advice on BP and lipid management.

Kind regards,
Dr Marcus Feeney
note: New exertional chest heaviness mentioned in passing sets the urgency, not the BP and lipids; hard because the red flag is buried in a letter framed as a BP/lipid review.

text:
Dear Dr,

Mr Hamish Tolley, 57, had COVID-19 5 months ago. His cough has largely resolved apart from an occasional morning cough, and his exertional fatigue is steadily improving; he is back at work full time. CXR and spirometry are normal and SpO2 is 98%. He would like a specialist review to make sure there is no lasting lung damage.

Kind regards,
Dr Clara Webster
note: Improving post-viral symptoms with normal tests.

text:
Dear Dr,

Re: Brian O'Keefe, 61

Brian is a council groundsman with right knee osteoarthritis. Pain has steadily worsened over 2 years; he now struggles with ladders and kneeling and has had to take time off work. He has completed 12 weeks of physio and a weight-loss program (lost 8 kg), had a steroid injection in March with 6 weeks of benefit, and takes paracetamol SR and occasional meloxicam. X-ray: severe medial compartment narrowing with osteophytes. He is keen to discuss knee replacement.

Regards,
Dr Imogen Tate
note: Severe knee OA limiting work after failed conservative care: disability without risk of rapid deterioration.

text:
Dear Cardiology,

Re: Melissa Draper, 44

Melissa has had left-sided chest pain for 2 months, sharp, worse with twisting and lifting her toddler, and reproducible on palpation over the 4th and 5th costal cartilages. No exertional pattern. It started after she began a new gym program. ECG normal, troponin x2 negative at ED in September, and a stress echo last month was normal with good exercise capacity. Non-smoker, normal lipids. She remains worried because her mother has angina and has asked for a cardiologist's opinion.

Kind regards,
Dr Kieran Doyle
note: Musculoskeletal chest wall pain with a negative cardiac work-up; referral is for reassurance. Hard because 'chest pain' to cardiology invites over-triage.

text:
Hi team,

Lachlan Brierley, 34, accountant. 18 months of sudden-onset fast regular palpitations, now about twice a month, lasting 10 to 40 minutes, stopped by breath holding. One episode captured at a pharmacy: regular narrow complex tachycardia at 190. Never syncopal. Resting ECG normal, no pre-excitation. He has had to leave client meetings and is now anxious about an episode while driving. Would value assessment for EP study and ablation.

Cheers,
Dr Tom Ashby
note: Recurrent SVT causing functional disruption but haemodynamically tolerated, with no pre-excitation.

text:
Dear Dr,

Re: Colin Abernethy, 55

Colin reports 4 months of progressive weakness of his right hand, so that he can no longer do up buttons, and more recently cramps and twitching in both arms and calves. He has lost 6 kg. Exam: wasting of the right first dorsal interosseous and thenar eminence, widespread fasciculations, brisk reflexes in all limbs and an upgoing right plantar. No sensory loss. CK 410. No neck pain.

Regards,
Dr Leila Farouk
note: Progressive mixed upper and lower motor neuron signs with weight loss, suspicious for motor neurone disease.

text:
Dear Dermatologist,

URGENT referral please.

Re: Ms Courtney Jaeger, 30

Courtney has a 4 cm congenital pigmented naevus on her left thigh, present since birth. She and her mother say it has not changed in size, colour or shape, and photos in her file from 2015 and 2020 look identical to today. No itch or bleeding. Dermoscopy: symmetrical globular pattern. She saw a social media video about melanoma and is frightened. Please see her to reassure her.

Dr Mitchell Grey
note: A congenital naevus documented as unchanged for a decade with benign dermoscopy is routine; hard because the GP requests urgent review.

text:
Dear Doctor,

Re: Beryl Atkinson, 78

Beryl had a left total hip replacement in July after a fall and has recovered well with physiotherapy; the orthopaedic team were happy at her 6-week review. She uses a stick outdoors and has had no further falls. The reason I am writing is her tremor. She has had a hand tremor for many years, but over the last 6 months it has worsened so that she spills tea, cannot write cheques and is embarrassed eating out. Exam: bilateral postural and action tremor, mild head tremor, no rigidity or bradykinesia. Propranolol is limited by low BP.

Dr Jacob Steiner
note: Worsening essential tremor now causing disability is semi-urgent neurology; hard because most of the letter is about the hip replacement and falls.

text:
Dear Dr,

Re: Chloe Ambrose, 27

Chloe had a soft systolic murmur noted at a pre-employment medical. She is entirely asymptomatic, plays netball twice weekly, and has no palpitations, syncope or family history of cardiac disease. Examination: grade 2/6 mid-systolic murmur at the left sternal edge, normal second heart sound, no other findings. ECG normal. I'd appreciate a non-urgent review and echo to characterise the murmur.

Kind regards,
Dr Jun Watanabe
note: Asymptomatic soft murmur in a fit young woman with a normal ECG; the GP's non-urgent request matches.

text:
Dear Respiratory Physician,

Re: Raymond Duggan, 63

Raymond is a current smoker (45 pack-years) who has coughed up blood-streaked sputum several times over the past 3 weeks, and once about a teaspoon of fresh blood. He has a long-standing smoker's cough but says it has changed, and he has lost 4 kg. CXR: right hilar fullness, no consolidation. CT chest requested. Hb 139, platelets and INR normal, not on anticoagulants. Please see him urgently.

Dr Gillian Pratt
note: Haemoptysis with weight loss and a hilar abnormality in a heavy smoker; the GP's urgent request matches.

text:
Dear Doctor,

Mrs Elsie Carmody, 84, lives in residential aged care. Over 3 weeks she has developed widespread intensely itchy red plaques on her trunk and limbs, and in the last week tense fluid-filled blisters up to 3 cm on her thighs and forearms, some burst and weeping. Oral mucosa clear. Linagliptin was started 6 months ago. Afebrile, eating and drinking. Nursing staff are dressing the erosions. I suspect bullous pemphigoid and have started potent topical steroids.

Dr Ross Kingsley
note: Widespread blistering in a frail elderly woman (suspected bullous pemphigoid) can deteriorate quickly.

text:
To the Orthopaedic Clinic,

Mrs Rosa Camilleri, 72. Left hip osteoarthritis, now severe, with rest and night pain most nights. Walking is limited to 100 m with a stick and she has difficulty with stairs and getting in and out of the car. She has stopped volunteering at the op shop. Paracetamol, celecoxib and a hydrotherapy course gave little relief. X-ray: superolateral joint space loss, bone on bone. BMI 31, HbA1c 6.6. She would like to be considered for hip replacement.

Yours faithfully,
Dr Anthony Reid
note: Severe hip OA with night pain and functional loss; significant disability but not likely to deteriorate quickly.

text:
Re: Margaret Oyelaran DOB 14/03/1954

Margaret (71) reports 4 weeks of increasing breathlessness, now short of breath after one flight of stairs, needing three pillows at night and waking breathless twice this week. Bilateral pitting oedema to mid-shin, weight up 4 kg. NT-proBNP 3,400 ng/L. CXR: cardiomegaly and small bilateral effusions. ECG: sinus 96, LBBB (not present in 2022). No previous cardiac history. I have started frusemide 40 mg daily. Please see her urgently.

Meds: amlodipine 5 mg, metformin 1 g bd, frusemide 40 mg mane.

Dr Ian Kowalczyk
note: New heart failure symptoms with raised NT-proBNP and new LBBB; the GP's urgent request matches the clinical picture.

text:
Re: Kiara Thompson, 31

Kiara had erythema nodosum and ankle swelling 2 months ago, now settled. CXR showed bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy. She has a mild dry cough but no breathlessness, weight loss or night sweats. Serum ACE raised, calcium normal, spirometry normal, eye review normal. She works as a primary school teacher and is otherwise well. Would appreciate assessment and confirmation of suspected sarcoidosis.

Dr Felix Grant
note: Probable Lofgren-type sarcoidosis with mild symptoms; needs confirmation within months.

text:
Dear Dr,

Re: Thomas Nakamura, 22

Thomas has severe allergic asthma managed by the respiratory clinic; he is now well controlled on budesonide/formoterol with no admissions this year, and his respiratory physician is not planning changes. I am referring him for his atopic eczema, which has worsened over the past year: widespread flexural and facial involvement, EASI around 24, frequent excoriation and two episodes of impetigo. Daily emollients, potent topical steroids and wet wraps have not given control. His sleep is badly disturbed and he is struggling at university.

Dr Imran Qureshi
note: Severe atopic eczema failing topical therapy is semi-urgent dermatology; hard because the letter opens with severe asthma and a respiratory clinic.

text:
Re: Liam O'Sullivan, 19

Moderate to severe inflammatory acne of the face, chest and back for 3 years, with early atrophic scarring on the cheeks. He failed 6 months of doxycycline 100 mg with adapalene/benzoyl peroxide gel, and a second 3-month course gave no lasting benefit. His mood is affected and he avoids social events, but has no suicidal ideation. He cannot afford private dermatology. Please assess for isotretinoin.

Dr Chloe Barrett
note: Scarring acne failing antibiotics needs isotretinoin assessment within months.

text:
Dear Neurology,

Mr Hamid Rezaei, 45, had a right Bell's palsy 14 months ago treated with prednisolone. He has recovered most function but has mild residual weakness of eye closure and some synkinesis (the eye narrows when he smiles). No other neurological symptoms; MRI at the time was normal. Eye protection is adequate. He would like an opinion on whether further treatment, such as facial physiotherapy or botulinum toxin, might help.

Regards,
Dr Siobhan Kerr
note: Stable residual deficit after Bell's palsy; cosmetic and minor functional issues only.

text:
Re: Ava Lindgren, 24

Three months of loose stools 4 to 5 times a day with intermittent crampy abdominal pain and occasional mucus, no blood. Weight stable, afebrile. Faecal calprotectin 460, repeated at 390. CRP 12, Hb 121, ferritin 18. Stool cultures, ova and parasites, and coeliac serology negative. No recent travel or antibiotics. I suspect inflammatory bowel disease. She is coping with loperamide.

Dr Matthew Kerr
note: Suspected IBD with raised calprotectin but stable weight and no bleeding; needs diagnosis within months.

text:
Re: Mrs Norma Fielding, 69

Ex-smoker (quit 2010, 40 pack-years). A CT chest done for persistent cough after a chest infection shows a 22 mm spiculated nodule in the left upper lobe, with no mediastinal lymphadenopathy. No previous imaging for comparison. The cough has now settled; no haemoptysis and weight stable. FEV1 1.8 L (72% predicted). Would appreciate review and further work-up.

Dr Marco Vitale
note: Spiculated 22 mm lung nodule in a heavy ex-smoker: suspected lung cancer.

text:
Re: Linh Pham, 44

Chronic hepatitis B (HBeAg negative), monitored by me for 6 years with normal ALT. Over the last 9 months ALT has risen from 38 to 61 and is now 84. HBV DNA 25,000 IU/mL (previously under 2,000). Ultrasound: no focal lesion, normal liver texture. AFP normal. No alcohol. Would appreciate assessment regarding antiviral therapy. Vietnamese interpreter required.

Dr Peter Vo
note: Chronic hepatitis B with rising ALT and viral load; needs treatment assessment within months.

text:
Re: Nina Kovacevic, 36, ICU nurse

Six months of twitching in her calves and occasionally her eyelid, worse with caffeine and after night shifts. No weakness, wasting, cramps, or swallowing or speech problems. Exam: occasional calf fasciculations, normal power, tone, reflexes and sensation. CK, electrolytes, magnesium and TFTs normal. She is anxious about motor neurone disease, having nursed patients with it, and would like a neurologist's opinion.

Dr Mark Delaney
note: Benign fasciculations with a normal exam and bloods; reassurance only.

text:
Re: Mai Tran, 44

De Quervain's tenosynovitis of the right wrist for 7 months. Pain over the radial styloid with thumb use, positive Finkelstein's test, ultrasound confirms thickened first extensor compartment with a septum. Two steroid injections (March and July) each gave about 6 weeks of relief. Thumb spica splint at work. She is a nail technician and has had to cut her hours by half. Requesting surgical opinion regarding release.

Dr George Papas
note: De Quervain's tenosynovitis failing injections and limiting work; dysfunction without risk of deterioration.

text:
Dear Orthopaedic Registrar,

Re: Ethan Marsh, 16 (DOB 02/08/2010)

Ethan has 6 weeks of right knee pain, now waking him at night and not relieved by ibuprofen. No injury. His mum has noticed a firm swelling above the knee. Afebrile, mildly limping. X-ray right femur: ill-defined lytic lesion in the distal femoral metaphysis with periosteal reaction; the radiologist queries a 'sunburst' appearance. ALP raised, CRP normal. I am concerned about a primary bone tumour. Please see urgently.

Dr Sanjay Pillai
note: Suspected primary bone sarcoma on X-ray in an adolescent with night pain; the GP's urgent request matches.

text:
Dear Dr,

Ms Renee Watkins, 35, has had asthma since childhood, poorly controlled for 12 months despite budesonide/formoterol 400/12 bd plus tiotropium. She needed three courses of oral prednisolone this year and had one ED visit without admission. Inhaler technique checked and adherence confirmed by dispensing records. Blood eosinophils 0.6. Sensitised to house dust mite. Would appreciate assessment for biologic therapy.

Regards,
Dr Paolo Ricci
note: Poorly controlled asthma on high-dose therapy with repeated steroid courses; needs specialist review within months.

text:
Re: Philip Durand, 60

Philip is worried about his memory since his mother developed Alzheimer's disease at 78. He reports occasional difficulty recalling names and misplacing his keys, but he continues to work full time as a lawyer and manages his finances. His wife has no concerns. MoCA 28/30. B12, TFTs and calcium normal. Mood mildly low. He would like a specialist assessment for reassurance and to discuss his own risk.

Dr Ellen Burke
note: Subjective memory concerns with normal cognitive screening and preserved function.

text:
Dear Cardiology,

Anita Srinivasan, 59, was diagnosed with paroxysmal AF in March. She is anticoagulated with apixaban 5 mg bd (CHA2DS2-VA 2) and rate controlled on metoprolol 50 mg bd. Despite this she has episodes of palpitations and fatigue lasting several hours roughly weekly, which are affecting her work as a school teacher. Echo: normal LV, mildly dilated left atrium. TFTs normal. She is interested in discussing rhythm control options, including ablation.

Thank you,
Dr Rebecca Hollis
note: Symptomatic paroxysmal AF already anticoagulated and rate controlled; referral is for rhythm-control options, not a deteriorating condition.

text:
Re: Craig Bennett, 46

Chronic plaque psoriasis for 15 years, worse over the past year and now involving about 12% of his body surface (elbows, knees, scalp, lower back, shins), PASI 14. He has failed betamethasone dipropionate, calcipotriol/betamethasone foam and coal tar. Phototherapy is not practical as he works fly-in fly-out. Some morning stiffness but no swollen joints. Significant impact on mood and relationships. Would appreciate assessment for systemic therapy.

Dr Joel Ainsworth
note: Moderate psoriasis failing topical treatment.

text:
Dear Dr Varga,

Please see urgently. Mr Neville Choi, 49, had a CT chest for a persistent cough (now resolved), which incidentally noted a mildly dilated ascending aorta, 41 mm. He is normotensive (124/78), has no connective tissue features and no family history of aortic disease. Echo confirms aortic root 40 mm, tricuspid aortic valve, normal LV. He is very anxious about this finding and has been reading about it online.

I'd appreciate advice on surveillance and BP targets.

Regards,
Dr Shona McAllister
note: Mild ascending aortic dilatation (40-41 mm) in a normotensive man needs surveillance only; hard because the GP asks for urgent review on account of anxiety, which the clinical content does not support.

text:
Re: Arthur Penrose, 70

Six weeks of increasing breathlessness, right-sided chest ache and 7 kg weight loss. Former boilermaker with asbestos exposure in the 1970s. CXR: moderate right pleural effusion, new since 2023. Afebrile, CRP 18. Not breathless at rest, SpO2 95%. No pleural tap yet. Meds: amlodipine, aspirin. I am concerned about mesothelioma or another malignancy.

Dr Wendy Hu
note: Unexplained unilateral effusion with weight loss and asbestos exposure: suspected malignancy.

text:
Dear Doctor,

Re: Sharon Mayes, 50

Sharon has had abdominal bloating and distension most days for 5 years, worse in the evening and relieved by passing wind. Bowel habit regular. No weight loss, bleeding, anaemia or nocturnal symptoms. Bloods, coeliac serology and calprotectin normal; iFOBT negative this year; abdominal and pelvic ultrasound and CA-125 normal. Low-FODMAP diet gave partial benefit. She is worried about cancer since a friend's diagnosis and would like specialist review.

Dr Rhys Gallant
note: Long-standing functional bloating with normal investigations and no alarm features.

text:
Dear Dermatology,

Mr Joseph Mensah, 26, developed a keloid on his central chest at the site of an acne lesion 2 years ago. It has slowly enlarged to 3 cm and is itchy at times but not painful. Silicone gel sheets have not helped much. He would like to discuss intralesional steroid or other options.

Kind regards,
Dr Ruth Abernathy
note: Symptomatic but benign keloid; minimal dysfunction.

text:
Dear Doctor,

Josephine Wallace, 68, ex-smoker (quit 2005, 20 pack-years), has had gradually increasing breathlessness over 6 to 8 months, now breathless walking up the hill to the shops. No chest pain, cough or wheeze. I initially suspected COPD, but spirometry is normal (FEV1/FVC 0.78) and CXR is clear. NT-proBNP 620. Echo: LVEF 55%, grade II diastolic dysfunction, moderate mitral regurgitation, mild LA dilatation. Symptoms have been stable over the last two months.

Meds: irbesartan 300 mg, atorvastatin 20 mg.

Regards,
Dr Simon Okafor
note: Stable breathlessness with normal spirometry and echo showing moderate MR and diastolic dysfunction is cardiac and semi-urgent; hard because a breathless ex-smoker looks respiratory.

text:
Re: Daniel Whitmore, 28

Gradual hair thinning at the temples and crown over 4 years, with a strong family history in his father and brothers. No scalp itch, scaling or patchy loss. FBC, ferritin and TFTs normal. Topical minoxidil for a year has helped somewhat but he dislikes the greasiness. No other medical history. He would like a specialist opinion on oral treatment options.

Dr Georgia Pappas
note: Androgenetic alopecia; cosmetic concern with no medical risk.

text:
Dear Dr,

Ian Dunstan, 66, has a nodule and early cord in his left palm at the base of the little finger, developing slowly over 3 years. Fixed flexion at the MCP joint is about 15 degrees; he can still place his hand flat on the table. No pain. His father had the same condition. He has heard about surgery and would like an opinion on when intervention would be appropriate.

Regards,
Dr Kate Olsen
note: Early Dupuytren's with a negative tabletop test; no functional loss yet.

text:
Dear Cardiologist,

Mr Darren Fitzgibbon, 45, is well and asymptomatic but is worried after his brother had a heart attack at 47 and his father had bypass surgery at 58. He is a non-smoker, BMI 29, BP 132/84. Total cholesterol 6.2, LDL 4.1, HDL 1.0. Five-year CVD risk on the Australian calculator is 6%. ECG normal. He would like an opinion on further risk stratification, such as a CT calcium score, and whether he should start a statin.

Regards,
Dr Amira Haddad
note: Asymptomatic cardiovascular risk assessment for family history; no active disease.

text:
Re: Jake Morrison, 28

Intermittent bright red blood on the paper after straining for 6 months, especially when constipated. No change in bowel habit, no weight loss and no family history of bowel cancer. PR: non-tender, no masses; small internal haemorrhoids seen on proctoscopy. Hb 152. Improved with fibre but still bothers him. Would appreciate review and consideration of banding.

Dr Owen Whitfield
note: Low-risk outlet bleeding from haemorrhoids in a young man with normal Hb.

text:
Dear Dr,

Re: Angela Mancini, 43

Chronic spontaneous urticaria for 8 months: daily itchy wheals lasting under 24 hours, with occasional lip swelling but never throat or breathing involvement. She has been on cetirizine 10 mg four times daily for 3 months with partial control. FBC, TSH and CRP normal; thyroid antibodies positive. Her sleep is poor from itch. Would appreciate assessment for omalizumab.

Regards,
Dr Harvey Quist
note: Chronic urticaria uncontrolled on high-dose antihistamines, with no airway involvement.

text:
Re: Holly Marchetti, 35

Holly has over 100 naevi and her mother had a melanoma at 52. She has not noticed any changing lesions, and my full skin check today with dermoscopy found nothing suspicious. Fair skin, burns easily. I would appreciate baseline total-body photography and advice on the frequency and setting of her ongoing surveillance. She works outdoors as a landscape gardener.

Dr Andrew Zhou
note: High-risk patient for surveillance planning with no suspicious lesion found.

text:
Dear Dr,

Mr Raymond Fox, 45, accountant, has mild hand dermatitis, mainly dryness and fine cracks on the fingertips in winter. It responds to regular moisturiser and a short course of mometasone. No work time lost and no vesicles or infection. He wonders whether patch testing would identify a trigger, as he recently changed hand soap.

Regards,
Dr Celia Wong
note: Mild intermittent hand dermatitis well controlled with simple measures.

text:
Re: Glenys Watt, 70

Glenys had a right mastectomy for breast cancer in 2018 and has been in remission. She has 3 weeks of right groin and thigh pain, worse on weight bearing, and is now using a walking stick. No fall. X-ray right femur: lucent lesion in the subtrochanteric region with cortical thinning, suspicious for metastasis. Calcium 2.71. I have also contacted her oncologist. I am concerned about an impending pathological fracture.

Dr Joanne Sutcliffe
note: Suspected femoral metastasis with impending pathological fracture.

text:
Dear Dr,

Re: Isaac Turnbull, 22

Isaac had a concussion playing Australian rules football 4 months ago, with brief loss of consciousness and a normal CT. His headaches and poor concentration have steadily improved and are now mild, about twice a week. He is back at university full time and sleeping well. Neurological examination is normal. He and his coach would like specialist advice on returning to contact sport.

Kind regards,
Dr Rachel Steed
note: Resolving post-concussion symptoms with a normal exam; advice on return to sport.

text:
Re: Zoe Hammond, 29

Chronic migraine: 16 headache days per month, 10 of them migrainous, for over a year. She has failed propranolol (fatigue), amitriptyline (weight gain) and topiramate 100 mg (cognitive side effects), and uses triptans 8 days a month. She misses about 3 days of work a month as a pharmacy assistant. Neurological exam and fundi normal; MRI brain 2024 normal. Would appreciate review for CGRP therapy or botulinum toxin.

Dr Bridget Lowry
note: Migraine not controlled after three preventives, with work impact and a normal exam.

text:
Headaches. Please see.

Re: Corey Adams, 33

Thanks for seeing this man with headaches. He has had them for some time. Panadol helps a bit. Exam OK. No significant past history. He works as a warehouse supervisor, is a non-smoker and drinks socially. He would like an opinion. No other details recorded today.

Meds: nil regular.
Allergies: NKDA.

Thanks,
Dr S. Patel
note: No duration, pattern or red flags are described and the exam is reported normal, so routine by default; hard because the letter has almost no clinical information.

text:
To the Cardiology Outpatient Clinic

Mrs Yvonne Petersen, 56, has noticed 'skipped beats' for about a year, mostly in the evening when resting. No dizziness, chest pain or breathlessness. 24-hour Holter: sinus rhythm with isolated ventricular ectopics, burden 0.4%, no runs. Echo: normal structure and function. TFTs and electrolytes normal. She has cut down on caffeine with some improvement. She has asked for a specialist opinion for reassurance.

Thank you
Dr Graham Tully
note: Low-burden ectopics with normal echo and Holter in a woman with no other symptoms; reassurance only.

text:
Re: Grace O'Neill, 52

Never smoker with no occupational exposures. A CT coronary angiogram showed an incidental 4 mm solid nodule in the right lower lobe. She is asymptomatic, with no cough, haemoptysis or weight loss. Guidelines suggest no follow-up is needed for a low-risk patient with a nodule this size, but she would like specialist reassurance before accepting this.

Dr Hilary Benton
note: Small incidental nodule in a low-risk never smoker; no follow-up needed.

text:
Re: Priyanka Desai, 37

Vitiligo on the hands and around the mouth for 8 years, with no new patches in the last 2 years. Using tacrolimus ointment with slight repigmentation. Thyroid function and HbA1c are normal. She feels self-conscious in summer and uses sunscreen daily. She would like to discuss phototherapy or the newer topical treatments she has read about.

Dr Liam Hartley
note: Stable vitiligo; treatment options discussion.

text:
Rash. Please see.

Re: Brodie King, 40

Thanks for seeing Brodie, who has a rash. He has had it for a while and tried a cream from the chemist. Otherwise well.

PMH: nil. Meds: nil. NKDA.
Smoker 10/day. Works as a plumber.
Married, two kids. No pets.
FHx: not known.
Alcohol: weekends.
No photos provided with this letter.

Thanks,
Dr L. Tran
note: No site, duration or features of the rash are given and he is well, so routine by default; hard because the letter has almost no clinical information.

text:
Dear Doctor,

Nathan Achterberg, 29, twisted his left knee playing indoor soccer 3 months ago. He has persisting medial joint line pain and the knee has caught and briefly locked on 4 occasions, freeing itself when he wiggles it. Small effusion, positive McMurray's. MRI: complex tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus with a flap; ACL intact. Six weeks of physio without improvement. He works as a chef and is on his feet all day.

Thanks,
Dr Rhiannon Price
note: Symptomatic meniscal tear with intermittent mechanical symptoms that resolve; impairs work but the knee is not locked.

text:
Dear Doctor,

Re: Simon Oduro, 46

Simon has generalised anxiety and insomnia, which have improved since we changed his sertraline to escitalopram in August; he now sees a psychologist fortnightly and his sleep is better with CBT-I. The reason for referral is his cough: a dry cough for 4 months that started after a cold and has not settled. Never smoker, no ACE inhibitor, no reflux symptoms. CXR and spirometry with reversibility normal. No weight loss or haemoptysis. A 6-week trial of inhaled corticosteroid did not help. It keeps him and his wife awake.

Dr Natalie Forde
note: Chronic cough without red flags after first-line tests is semi-urgent respiratory; hard because most of the letter is about anxiety and insomnia.

text:
Re: Cyril Mackenzie, 78

Renal transplant 2009, on tacrolimus and mycophenolate, with multiple previous SCCs. A new lesion on the back of his right hand appeared about 5 weeks ago and has grown quickly into a 15 mm tender keratotic nodule with a central crater. No palpable axillary or epitrochlear nodes. I suspect SCC, possibly keratoacanthoma type. Would appreciate review for excision.

Dr Tamsin Reilly
note: Rapidly growing suspected SCC in an immunosuppressed transplant recipient.

text:
Re: Natasha Bell, 39

Hepatic steatosis was noted incidentally on an ultrasound done for renal colic. LFTs are normal and FIB-4 is 0.7. BMI 30, no diabetes, minimal alcohol. She has started a weight-loss program with a dietitian and has lost 3 kg. She would like a specialist opinion on what this means for her and whether any monitoring is needed.

Dr Clare Dunbar
note: Incidental fatty liver with low fibrosis risk and normal LFTs.

text:
Dear Dr,

URGENT please. Mr Dimitri Stavros, 51, truck driver, has had mechanical low back pain for over 10 years, flaring a few times a year. The current flare is 3 weeks old and similar to previous ones. No leg pain below the knee, no numbness or weakness, bladder and bowel normal, no weight loss or fever, and no history of cancer. Neurological examination normal. MRI: multilevel degenerative disc disease without nerve compression. He is frustrated and wants to know if surgery could fix it.

Dr Wendy Albright
note: Chronic mechanical back pain with no red flags or neurological signs is routine; hard because the GP marks it urgent.

text:
Dear Dr,

Re: Emma Fitzroy, 36

Emma has had IBS with constipation and bloating since her teens, unchanged in pattern. Symptoms are mild and controlled with psyllium and a modified diet. No weight loss, bleeding or nocturnal symptoms, and no family history of bowel cancer or IBD. FBC, CRP and coeliac serology normal; calprotectin 22. She has moved to the area and would like a gastroenterologist to confirm the diagnosis and advise on long-term management.

Kind regards,
Dr Victoria Nolan
note: Long-standing stable IBS with normal tests and no alarm features.

text:
Re: Diane Kowalski, 55

Diane has had a painful, stiff right shoulder for 7 months with no injury. She has type 2 diabetes. External rotation is markedly restricted (10 degrees versus 60 on the left). An ultrasound-guided steroid injection with hydrodilatation in June gave partial relief only, and physio progress has plateaued. Sleep is disturbed and she has difficulty dressing and doing her hair. X-ray normal. I would appreciate assessment regarding further options.

Dr Lauren Mitchell
note: Adhesive capsulitis failing injection and physio with marked functional impact, but not likely to deteriorate.

text:
Re: Roger Halloran, 61

Barrett's oesophagus (3 cm, no dysplasia) on gastroscopy 3 years ago. On pantoprazole 40 mg daily with reflux well controlled. No dysphagia, weight loss or anaemia. Non-smoker, BMI 28. Due for surveillance endoscopy; his previous gastroenterologist has left the region and he would like his surveillance continued at the hospital clinic. Hb and ferritin normal this year.

Dr Thea Mulligan
note: Scheduled surveillance of non-dysplastic Barrett's oesophagus.

text:
Re: Gareth Lewis, 49

Office worker with loud snoring, apnoeas witnessed by his wife and an Epworth score of 14. BMI 36, treated hypertension. He is not a commercial driver and has had no drowsy driving incidents. A home sleep study is not affordable for him. Would appreciate a sleep study and assessment for obstructive sleep apnoea.

Dr Fern Gallagher
note: Probable moderate OSA with daytime sleepiness but no driving risk.

text:
Abdo pain on and off.

Pls review. Thanks.

Pt: Brandon Kelly, 31. Pain in the tummy, comes and goes. Bloods normal. Has tried Buscopan, not sure if it helped. No other history recorded. Unclear where the pain is or how long it has been going on.

PMH: asthma.
Meds: Ventolin prn, Symbicort.
NKDA. Lives with partner, works in IT.

Dr J. Okonkwo
note: Intermittent abdominal pain in a young man with normal bloods and no red flags described, so routine; hard because location, duration, bowel habit and weight are all missing.

text:
Dear Dr,

Re: Gwen Holloway, 64

Gwen has had 14 months of burning, numb feet, gradually ascending to mid-calf, with pain disturbing her sleep. Exam: stocking sensory loss to mid-calf, absent ankle jerks, normal power. HbA1c 5.6; B12, folate, TFTs, SPEP, renal and liver function normal. Alcohol minimal. Pregabalin 75 mg bd is partially helpful. I'd appreciate further assessment and nerve conduction studies.

Regards,
Dr Fraser Doherty
note: Slowly progressive painful sensory neuropathy without weakness; causes disability but is not changing quickly.

text:
Dear Doctor,

Ms Louise Carter, 34, has mild erythematotelangiectatic rosacea of the cheeks for 3 years, flushing with heat and wine. Azelaic acid gel and daily sunscreen give reasonable control. No papules, pustules or eye symptoms. She works in hospitality and finds the flushing embarrassing. She would like advice on vascular laser and whether anything else might help.

Regards,
Dr Mehmet Arslan
note: Mild rosacea controlled on topical therapy.

text:
Dear Dr,

Re: Graham Spencer, 69

Mild bilateral hand tremor for over 10 years, noticeable when holding a newspaper. It has not changed over the last few years and does not interfere with eating, writing or his woodwork. It improves with a glass of wine, and his mother had a similar tremor. Exam: low-amplitude postural tremor, no rest tremor, no rigidity. TSH normal. He would like confirmation of the diagnosis and does not want medication.

Kind regards,
Dr Alice Monro
note: Mild, stable essential tremor without functional impact.

text:
Dear Dr,

Re: Steven Kouris, 54

Please review re heart. He has had some palpitations on and off. ECG in rooms was OK. He is otherwise fit and well and keen to get it checked out. He works as a courier and is busy. No other medical history of note. Blood tests done last year were normal.

Meds: nil.

Thanks,
Dr Paul Ingram
note: Intermittent palpitations with a normal ECG and no red flags described, so routine by default; hard because the letter omits frequency, triggers and associated symptoms.

text:
Dear Dr Gallo,

Re: Helena Marsh, 62

Helena has had migraine with visual aura since her twenties; attacks are now less frequent, about one a month, and respond to sumatriptan. I would value your advice on whether she should continue pizotifen. She also told me that 10 days ago she had a 20-minute episode of numbness and clumsiness of the left face and arm, without visual symptoms or headache, quite unlike her usual aura. It resolved fully. She has hypertension and smokes. Examination today is normal.

Kind regards,
Dr Craig Holt
note: A new transient focal deficit unlike her aura in a hypertensive smoker of 62 is a possible TIA; hard because it is buried in a migraine medication review.

text:
Re: Marcus Leota, 33

Marcus tore his right ACL playing rugby 6 years ago and was managed without surgery. He has had no episodes of giving way since and the knee is stable for running and gym work. He is considering returning to social touch football and would like advice on whether reconstruction is advisable. Exam: Lachman grade 1 with a firm end point, no effusion, full range.

Dr Yasmin Chaudhry
note: Old ACL injury with a functionally stable knee; advice only.

text:
Dear Gastroenterologist,

Re: Kevin Moffat, 72

Kevin has iron deficiency anaemia: Hb 98 (128 last year), MCV 74, ferritin 5. He has lost 7 kg over 4 months without trying and reports fatigue and breathlessness on exertion. No overt bleeding and bowel habit unchanged. Not on anticoagulants or NSAIDs. Coeliac serology negative. He has never had a colonoscopy and never returned his bowel screening kits. I have arranged IV iron. Category 1 referral please, for gastroscopy and colonoscopy.

Regards,
Dr Nadia Rossi
note: Iron deficiency anaemia with weight loss in an older man is a suspected GI cancer; the GP's category 1 request matches.

text:
Dear Gastroenterology,

Ms Rachel Duffy, 33, has a positive tTG-IgA of 86 U/mL (ULN 15) with normal total IgA, tested because of fatigue, bloating and mild iron deficiency (ferritin 14, Hb 124). She remains on a normal gluten-containing diet pending biopsy. Weight stable, no dysphagia or bleeding. Her sister has coeliac disease. I would be grateful for gastroscopy and duodenal biopsies to confirm the diagnosis.

Regards,
Dr Harriet Lowe
note: Positive coeliac serology needing confirmatory biopsy; symptomatic but not deteriorating.

text:
Dear Dermatology,

Mrs Gail Ferguson, 58, has multiple skin tags on the neck and in both axillae, gradually increasing over years. They occasionally catch on her necklace and bra straps. No changing pigmented lesions. Type 2 diabetes. She would like them removed, but there are too many for me to manage in the clinic. She is otherwise well.

Kind regards,
Dr Rory Patton
note: Benign skin tags; cosmetic and minor nuisance only.

text:
Re: Norman Astley, 68

Punch biopsy last week of a 9 mm pearly lesion on the left nasal ala: nodular basal cell carcinoma. It has been present for about a year, slowly enlarging and occasionally bleeding. Given the site, I think it needs specialist management, possibly Mohs surgery. Several previous truncal BCCs were excised in my rooms. Not on anticoagulants. A semi-urgent appointment would be appreciated.

Dr Lydia Ferris
note: Biopsy-proven nodular BCC on the nose: slow-growing but needs specialist surgery; the GP's semi-urgent request matches.

text:
Re: Leonard Pike, 69

Right ring finger triggering for 8 months. One steroid injection in May gave about 3 months of relief, and symptoms have returned but are mild: catching in the mornings only, unlocking easily, with no pain during the day. Type 2 diabetes, well controlled. He is happy to wait but would like a surgical opinion on release. Retired, and plays lawn bowls without trouble.

Dr Teresa Malouf
note: Mild trigger finger with minimal dysfunction.

text:
Re: Tony Kapoor, 56

Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. ALT 78, AST 66, platelets 142, FIB-4 2.9. Ultrasound: coarse echogenic liver with smooth outline, spleen 12.5 cm, no ascites. HbA1c 7.6, BMI 34. Alcohol 6 standard drinks a week. Hepatitis B and C serology negative; ferritin 410 with transferrin saturation 32%. Fibroscan is not available locally. Grateful for assessment for advanced fibrosis.

Dr Simone Achebe
note: Fatty liver disease with an indeterminate-to-high fibrosis score; needs assessment but is not decompensated.

text:
Re: Deborah Clancy, 52

Two years of an uncomfortable urge to move her legs in the evenings, relieved by walking. Sleep onset is delayed but she generally sleeps 6 to 7 hours. Ferritin 38 (oral iron started), renal function normal. Not on antidepressants. She has tried stretching and reducing caffeine with some benefit. Exam normal. Symptoms are mild and stable and she would like advice on longer-term management.

Dr Lisa Hargreaves
note: Mild stable restless legs syndrome with iron already being addressed.

text:
Dear Doctor,

Ms Sophie Andersen, 38, had ORIF of a right bimalleolar ankle fracture at your hospital in 2021. The fracture has united and she walks pain-free, but she notices the lateral plate when wearing ski boots and some hiking boots, causing mild irritation. Skin intact, no signs of infection. She would like to discuss removal of metalwork. X-ray: healed fracture, hardware intact.

Regards,
Dr Martin Hale
note: Elective removal of mildly irritating metalwork after a healed fracture.

text:
Re: Daniel Chua, 31

Known left temporal focal epilepsy since age 18, seizure-free for 4 years on levetiracetam 1 g bd. In the past 3 months he has had two focal aware seizures (rising epigastric sensation and deja vu, about 1 minute each) and no convulsive events. Adherence is good, no new medicines, but his sleep has been poor since his baby was born. He has stopped driving. Grateful for advice on medication adjustment.

Dr Natalie Bryce
note: Breakthrough focal aware seizures in established epilepsy with an obvious trigger; needs adjustment but is not escalating.

text:
Dear Dr,

Re: Omar Barakat, 28

Omar has mild asthma, using as-needed budesonide/formoterol 1 to 2 times a week, with no exacerbations in 3 years. Spirometry last month was normal and his inhaler technique is good. He is starting a job that requires respirator fit-testing and his employer has asked for a specialist letter confirming his asthma is controlled.

Kind regards,
Dr Ellie Sutton
note: Mild, stable asthma review for paperwork.

text:
Dear Dr,

Re: Tahlia Burgess, 26

Tahlia has relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis, diagnosed 2022, stable on ocrelizumab under Dr Hennessy at the MS clinic; her last MRI showed no new lesions and her neurological examination is unchanged. The reason for this referral is her right knee. She has had 3 lateral patellar dislocations in the past year, the latest in August, each reducing spontaneously. She now avoids stairs and has stopped her dance classes. MRI: trochlear dysplasia, MPFL disruption, no loose body. Four months of physio have not helped.

Regards,
Dr Owen Park
note: Recurrent patellar dislocation with functional limitation is semi-urgent orthopaedics; hard because the letter opens with stable MS, pulling towards neurology.

text:
Dear Respiratory Clinic,

Mr Frank Oakley, 71, ex-smoker, has COPD (GOLD 3, FEV1 42% predicted). He has had two exacerbations requiring prednisolone this year, neither needing admission. Breathlessness is mMRC 3 and has gradually worsened over 12 months. He has been on triple inhaled therapy since June and completed pulmonary rehab in 2023. SpO2 93% at rest. I would appreciate optimisation of his management and assessment of home oxygen eligibility.

Regards,
Dr Lucinda Crane
note: Worsening but stable severe COPD on maximal inhaled therapy.

text:
Re: Kenneth Rafter, 74

Numerous seborrhoeic keratoses on the back and chest, increasing over 10 years. They are stuck-on, waxy and brown, with typical features on dermoscopy, and none has changed quickly. Some itch when they catch on clothing. He would like a full skin check by a dermatologist for peace of mind, and advice on removal options.

Dr Nicole Ashdown
note: Typical seborrhoeic keratoses without suspicious change.

text:
Re: Stanley Oduya, 69

Two weeks of painless jaundice with dark urine, pale stools and itch. Lost 6 kg over 2 months with poor appetite. New diagnosis of diabetes in August (HbA1c 8.4). Bilirubin 142, ALP 520, GGT 610, ALT 180. Ultrasound: dilated intra- and extrahepatic ducts, CBD 12 mm, pancreatic head poorly seen. Afebrile and well in himself. CT pancreas protocol booked.

Dr Erin Matthews
note: Painless obstructive jaundice with weight loss and new diabetes: suspected pancreatic cancer.

text:
Dear Neurologist,

Please see urgently.

Mrs Tanya Bellamy, 48, had an MRI brain for her long-standing tension-type headaches, which showed 'a few scattered non-specific T2 hyperintensities in the frontal white matter, likely small vessel or migrainous'. She has never had visual loss, numbness, weakness or balance problems, and neurological examination is normal. Her headaches are unchanged. She has read about multiple sclerosis online and is very distressed, which is why I am asking for an early appointment.

Dr Caroline Webb
note: Incidental non-specific white matter changes with a normal exam and no demyelinating symptoms are routine; hard because the GP requests urgent review due to anxiety.

text:
Dear Doctor,

Mr Andrew Kovacs, 52, fell from a ladder 10 days ago, landing on his outstretched right arm. Since then he cannot lift the arm above shoulder height, although passive range is full. No neurovascular deficit. X-ray: no fracture or dislocation. Ultrasound yesterday: full-thickness tears of supraspinatus and infraspinatus with 3 cm retraction. He is right-handed and works as a carpenter. Grateful for assessment for possible repair.

Regards,
Dr Helen Fong
note: Acute traumatic massive rotator cuff tear in a working-age man; repair outcomes depend on early surgery.

text:
Dear Dr,

I would be grateful if you could see Jackson Tuiasosopo, 19, who plays rugby league at state level and collapsed during sprint training last Saturday. He describes his chest pounding, then losing consciousness for about 30 seconds, recovering fully. A similar near-faint occurred during a game in July. His uncle died suddenly at 31, cause unknown. Examination normal, no murmur. ECG: sinus rhythm, QTc 455 ms, voltage criteria for LVH with lateral T wave inversion. I have advised him to stop all sport until reviewed.

Regards,
Dr Hannah Moretti
Riverside Family Practice
note: Exertional syncope with a family history of sudden death and an abnormal ECG: possible inherited cardiac condition.

text:
Dear Doctor,

Re: Sandra Ivanova, 58

Sandra has had increasing breathlessness over 2 months, now short of breath walking 50 m on the flat, with a dry cough. I initially wondered about heart failure, but echo is normal (LVEF 60%, normal RV pressures) and NT-proBNP is normal. Exam: fine bibasal inspiratory crackles and finger clubbing. SpO2 96% at rest, falling to 88% walking in the corridor. CXR: bilateral basal reticular shadowing. Spirometry restrictive. Never smoker; worked in a timber mill.

Dr Hugh Sanderson
note: Rapidly progressive fibrotic lung disease with exertional desaturation after cardiac causes are excluded; hard because the work-up started as cardiac.

text:
SOB. ?asthma. Pls assess.

Pt: Jessica Moore, 25. Has been getting short of breath sometimes, not sure how often or what sets it off, or whether there is wheeze. Ventolin from the chemist maybe helps. Non-smoker. Exam normal today. No spirometry done yet.

PMH: hay fever.
Meds: Ventolin prn, loratadine.
NKDA. Works in hospitality.
FHx: not recorded. Social: lives with flatmates.

Dr C. Ferraro
note: Intermittent breathlessness in a young non-smoker with a normal exam and no red flags described, so routine; hard because frequency, triggers and test results are all missing.

text:
Dear Doctor,

Mr Callum Fraser, 24, tall and slim, had a left primary spontaneous pneumothorax 8 months ago, treated with aspiration, with full re-expansion on follow-up CXR. No recurrence. He stopped smoking afterwards and is otherwise well with no lung disease. He has been offered a scuba diving trip and is planning overseas flights, and would like specialist advice on the risks.

Regards,
Dr Imelda Ruiz
note: Resolved pneumothorax; advice about diving and flying.

text:
Dear Dr,

Re: Kwame Asante, 52

Hypertension diagnosed 2021, still poorly controlled despite good adherence (pharmacy-packed) to telmisartan 80 mg, amlodipine 10 mg and indapamide 2.5 mg. Clinic BP 168/102, ABPM daytime average 156/98. Renal function normal, potassium 3.6, aldosterone/renin ratio pending. Urine ACR mildly raised. ECG shows LVH by voltage. No headaches, visual change or chest pain. I'd appreciate your input on resistant hypertension work-up and management.

Yours sincerely,
Dr Louise Brandt
note: Resistant hypertension with early end-organ change needs specialist work-up within months, not weeks.

text:
Re: Desmond Hartigan, 66

Known IHD, LAD stent 2019. Now on bisoprolol 5 mg, ISMN 60 mg, aspirin and rosuvastatin 20 mg. Over the past 3 months he gets predictable chest tightness walking briskly for more than 15 minutes, relieved by GTN, once or twice a week. No rest pain and no change in pattern recently. Exercise tolerance otherwise reasonable; still playing bowls. ECG unchanged. Lipids at target. Would appreciate review of his anti-anginal therapy and whether further investigation is warranted.

Dr P. Nguyen
note: Stable angina on established treatment with a fixed threshold; needs review but is not expected to deteriorate quickly.

text:
Dear Dr,

Re: Ingrid Halvorsen, 54

Ingrid has had severe plaque psoriasis for 20 years, well controlled since starting methotrexate 15 mg weekly under the dermatology clinic 4 years ago; her skin is clear and she is very happy with treatment. Her ALT has been mildly raised on the last four tests (52, 58, 55, 60; ULN 40), stable over 12 months, with normal bilirubin and albumin. BMI 32, alcohol 2 drinks a week. Dermatology have asked for a hepatology opinion on fibrosis assessment and whether methotrexate can safely continue.

Dr Rowan Ellis
note: Stable mild ALT rise on methotrexate needing fibrosis assessment is routine gastroenterology; hard because psoriasis dominates the letter and may pull to dermatology.

Dear Dermatology,

Ms Kayla Robinson, 27, has hidradenitis suppurativa of both axillae and the groin, Hurley stage II, with painful nodules and abscesses every 2 to 3 weeks and sinus tracts in the left axilla. She has had 3 months of doxycycline and then clindamycin plus rifampicin, with only modest improvement. BMI 33, smoker trying to quit. She is missing shifts at the supermarket. Would appreciate review for biologic therapy.

Kind regards,
Dr Ella Fairbairn
note: Moderate hidradenitis failing oral antibiotics, painful and affecting work.

text:
Re: Ahmed Saleh, 57

Right trigeminal neuralgia (V2/V3) for 8 months: electric shock pain triggered by chewing and brushing his teeth. Carbamazepine 200 mg tds has reduced attacks by about half, but he gets dizziness at higher doses. He is eating soft food and has lost 2 kg. Neurological exam normal with no facial sensory loss. MRI brain requested. Would appreciate advice on alternative medication and whether he is a candidate for surgery.

Dr Ingrid Paulsen
note: Partially controlled trigeminal neuralgia with normal exam; significant pain but not a deteriorating condition.

text:
Dear Dermatologist,

Re: Barry Noonan, 61

Barry's wife noticed that a mole on his upper back has changed over the past 3 months. It is now 11 mm, asymmetrical with irregular borders and several shades of brown and black, with a raised nodular area at one edge that bled after he scratched it. He had a lot of sunburn as a lifeguard in his youth. No previous skin cancers. Dermoscopy: atypical network and blue-white veil. Photo attached.

Kind regards,
Dr Penelope Shaw
note: Rapidly changing pigmented lesion with nodularity and bleeding: suspected melanoma.

text:
Dear Dr,

Re: Patricia Lennox, 64

Patricia has bilateral hallux valgus, left more than right, slowly progressive over many years. She gets a mild ache in narrow shoes but is comfortable in wide-fitting footwear and walks 5 km daily. No skin breakdown. She has seen a podiatrist and has orthotics. X-rays: moderate hallux valgus bilaterally, HVA 30 degrees on the left. She would like to know whether surgery would be worthwhile in the future.

Thanks,
Dr Samuel Wright
note: Bunions with mild symptoms controlled by footwear; minimal dysfunction.

text:
Dear Doctor,

Re: Hayley Gordon, 41

Hayley has had heartburn and regurgitation for 18 months, worse at night. She has been on esomeprazole 40 mg twice daily for 3 months with only partial improvement, and has tried raising the head of the bed, intentional weight loss (5 kg) and avoiding late meals. No dysphagia, vomiting, unintended weight loss or anaemia (Hb 136). H. pylori breath test negative. Would appreciate gastroscopy and advice on further management.

Kind regards,
Dr Callum Rhodes
note: Reflux not responding to high-dose PPI, without alarm features.

text:
Dear Gastroenterology,

Ms Lauren Whitby, 45, has no bowel symptoms. Her father was diagnosed with colorectal cancer at 55 and her paternal aunt at 62. Bowel habit normal, no bleeding, and Hb and iron studies are normal. Her father's surgeon advised colonoscopic screening, and I'd be grateful if you could arrange this. She is otherwise well and on no regular medication.

Kind regards,
Dr Ben Hollister
note: Asymptomatic screening colonoscopy for family history.
